topic: Introduction to Topology: The Geometry of Rubber Sheets
target_audience: University students (non-math majors or early undergraduates)

sections.title: The Hook: Geometry vs. Topology
animations: Draw a circle, label it 'Geometry' in #FFFFFF.
Morph circle into an irregular shape, label 'Geometry' changes to #FF4500.
Display a triangle and square morphing into each other labeled 'Topology' #00CED1.
Highlight the preservation of object continuity.
Animate a mug warping into a donut shape.

sections.title: Prerequisite Concept: Homeomorphism
animations: Show two squares, label them 'Square' #FFFFFF and 'Circle' #FFFFFF.
Display an animation morphing the square into the circle smoothly.
Color the morphing path #32CD32 to indicate equivalence.
Display 'Homeomorphic' label #00CED1 when morphing completes.
Show prohibited action (a red X) when attempting to tear a shape.

sections.title: The Key Invariant: Genus (The 'Hole' Count)
animations: Display a sphere, label 'Genus 0' #FFFFFF.
Display a single torus, label 'Genus 1' #00FF00.
Display a double-torus, label 'Genus 2' #FF4500.
Pulse the holes in the shapes with #FFD700.
Arrange the objects side-by-side to compare genus count.

sections.title: The Famous Application: The Euler Characteristic
lecture_lines: Formula: Vertices minus edges plus faces.
Always equals two for convex polyhedra.
animations: Display V-E+F=2 formula in #FFFFFF.
Label V (Vertices) #FF4500, E (Edges) #00CED1, F (Faces) #32CD32.
Animate vertices appearing on a cube in #FF4500.
Animate edges connecting vertices in #00CED1.
Show the final sum '2' pulsing in #FFD700.

sections.title: Real-World Conclusion: Why Topology Matters
animations: Show a complex city map with connections.
Overlay a topological network graph in #00CED1.
Highlight optimal paths in the graph with a flowing movement in #FFD700.
